info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.Git as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.418.1): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. Generated by openvibe-contracts lib/openapi.js; do not edit.

get.summary: Read a repository on OpenVibe.Git (git.openvibe.codes): its row, tree, blob, raw file, commits, one commit with its diff, branches, tags, releases, contributors and insights.
get.description: **git.repo.read** (first-party): Read a repository on OpenVibe.Git (git.openvibe.codes): its row, tree, blob, raw file, commits, one commit with its diff, branches, tags, releases, contributors and insights. A public repository is read without a token. A private one needs its owner's session, a Git token made on the repository page, or a first-party service token (Codes, Run, Link) that holds this capability for the audience openvibe.git and names the person in X-OV-Subject. A private repository answers 404 to anyone who may not see it, never 403.

post.summary: Write on OpenVibe.Git (git.openvibe.codes): make a repository in a person's name, mint their short-lived Git token for clone and push, push a branch over HTTPS, write files on a branch without a clone
post.description: **git.repo.write** (first-party): Write on OpenVibe.Git (git.openvibe.codes): make a repository in a person's name, mint their short-lived Git token for clone and push, push a branch over HTTPS, write files on a branch without a clone, and set a release. The owner acts with their session; a first-party service token (Codes first) holds this capability for the audience openvibe.git and names the person in X-OV-Subject. A service may also write an official repository. Never another person's repository.

post.summary: Report commit statuses (checks) on OpenVibe.Git (git.openvibe.codes): POST /api/v1/repos/:owner/:name/commits/:sha/statuses with {context, state: pending|success|failure|error, description?, target_ur
post.description: **git.checks.write** (first-party): Report commit statuses (checks) on OpenVibe.Git (git.openvibe.codes): POST /api/v1/repos/:owner/:name/commits/:sha/statuses with {context, state: pending|success|failure|error, description?, target_url?}. A first-party CI service (Run first) holds this capability for the audience openvibe.git and reports any repository it builds; the owner may report their own. Reads (GET, the latest per context) need no capability on a public repository and git.repo.read on a private one. A change is mergeable only when its required contexts are green.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

git.access-request.v1.title: GitAccessRequest
git.access-request.v1.description: git.access-request@1: the common request of git.read and git.write on OpenVibe.Git. owner and name name the repository at git.openvibe.codes; ref and path pick what is read; branch, message and files describe a contents write without a clone. A service names the person it acts for in X-OV-Subject, not in this body.

owner.description: The repository owner's lower-case OpenVibe username.

name.description: The repository name, lower-case and never ending in .git.

ref.description: A branch or tag to read at; the default branch when absent.

path.description: A path inside the tree or a blob's path.

branch.description: The branch a contents write goes on.

message.description: The commit message of a contents write.

files.description: The files a contents write changes, by path and full content.

git.access-result.v1.title: GitAccessResult
git.access-result.v1.description: git.access-result@1: the common result of git.read and git.write on OpenVibe.Git. A repository names its full name, its page and clone addresses, its visibility and default branch; a contents write or a token also carries the branch or commit it made.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
